correctness.rationale: For the ordinary four-cut complex Δ4(P_n³), the full-ambient Alexander dual Kn consists of subsets whose every four-element subset is connected, exactly consecutive-gap ≤3. On n=8 the oriented join of triangle boundary on {1,2,8} with 4-cycle on {3,4,5,6} is an integral 3-cycle with 12 supported tetrahedra; all are Kn faces, verified independently by oriented boundary enumeration. The chosen Q=[1,3,5,8] has chain coefficient −1 and no five-vertex extension in K8; indicator cochain e_Q is closed and evaluates to −1 on the cycle, yielding primitive split Z in H³(K8;Z). For n≥8, clamp i↦min(i,8) preserves edges/connected four-tuples and retracts Kn onto K8. Split injection in integral cohomology persists. Alexander duality on the full [n] shifts i=n−6 to cohomological degree 3, strictly below pure top n−5. Nonvoidness follows from disconnected {1,2,3,n}. Pure shellability would prohibit next-to-top reduced homology. All dimensions, signs and n=8 endpoint checked.
residual_risks: The proof proves existence of a free summand only, not exact total Betti number or homotopy type.
Clamping is a genuine all-n simplicial retraction; finite enumeration n=8..13 only supplements its proof.

value.rationale: This is a structurally motivated sharp contrast to known shellability of squared path cut complexes: one step in path power and four-cut size gives a provably persistent, primitive integral next-to-top homology class. The explicit retraction converts a finite 8-vertex obstruction into an unbounded natural family; it supplies a non-shellability witness stronger than isolated computational evidence.
residual_risks: Does not classify complete homotopy type or torsion, but neither is needed for the proved obstruction.
